title: Career roadmap · Executive Professor
summary: Build an applied business-academic career that combines doctoral-level research with executive experience, teaching, industry engagement and evidence-based management practice.

facts.Current degree: D.Sc / D.Litt / DBA / Post-Doctoral & Industry-Sponsored Doctorates
facts.Course: Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) / Executive Doctorate
facts.Timeline assumption: A DBA/executive doctorate is already an advanced doctoral qualification. The next step is normally faculty, executive-education, applied-research or industry-academic work rather than another degree. “Executive Professor” is not a universally standard academic rank, so actual appointment titles and eligibility must be checked against each institution.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build a strong applied-research and teaching profile while maintaining credible executive/industry engagement.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Establish a recognised management niche such as strategy, finance, operations, entrepreneurship, technology management, HR or leadership.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead executive programmes, applied research centres, industry partnerships and doctoral/senior-management teaching.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become a senior practitioner-scholar who connects management research with boardroom and organisational decisions.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant
Not applicable. The DBA/executive-doctorate pathway is already at doctoral level. Additional development should focus on research, teaching, executive practice and institutional contribution.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: The executive-professor profile should remain dual-track: rigorous academic research plus genuine organisational experience. Continue working with executives, boards, companies or public organisations so teaching is grounded in current management problems rather than only historical cases.

At DBA level, conventional internships are usually inappropriate. The stronger equivalents are executive projects, consulting engagements, industry research partnerships and visiting-faculty opportunities.

blocks.text: Ph.D./advanced research routes
Since the student already has a DBA/executive doctorate:

The long-term profile should be that of a practitioner-scholar with an identifiable research agenda and substantial executive credibility. A senior executive professor should be able to teach advanced management, publish credible applied research, design executive programmes, advise organisations and build university-industry partnerships. The DBA should be used as the bridge between rigorous research and real organisational decision-making.
